number.why: The reported Cox HR and 95% CI match the served numbers for LCZ696 versus enalapril and the primary cardiovascular-death/HF-hospitalization composite, with follow-up up to 40 months. Agreement is with the numerical result in the stated FAS; the ruling correctly flags that unrestricted intention-to-treat is not established.

quotes.span: RESULT OUTCOME 1 ANALYSIS 0: groups LCZ696, Enalapril | Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.0881 (95% CI 0.6501 to 1.8212) | p 0.6260 | METHOD Regression, Cox

RESULT OUTCOME 1 [PRIMARY]: Exposure-adjusted Incident Rate (EAIR) of CEC Confirmed Composite Endpoints | DESCRIPTION: Composite endpoint is defined as either cardiovascular (CV) death or heart failure (HF) hospitalization in Japanese patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) and reduced ejection fraction.

TIME FRAME: up to 40 months | POPULATION: FAS consists of all randomized patients with the exception for those patients who have not been qualified for randomization and have not received investigational drug, but have been inadvertently randomized into the study.

The composite endpoint events occurred on and after EOS declaration were reported by investigators but those events were not required to be adjudicated by CEC and not included in the efficacy analysis.

entry.why: The entry criteria establish adults with symptomatic chronic HFrEF: minimum age 20 years, NYHA II-IV, and LVEF ≤35%. The source explicitly establishes the randomized, double-blind, active-controlled comparison of LCZ696 with enalapril.

missed: The follow-up binding needs an explicit efficacy cutoff: evidence/held/registry/NCT02468232.json states, "The composite endpoint events occurred on and after EOS declaration were reported by investigators but those events were not required to be adjudicated by CEC and not included in the efficacy analysis." Thus the estimate should be described as the pre-EOS efficacy analysis up to 40 months, rather than implying inclusion of every event through the longest follow-up. This qualification does not change the reported HR or entry ruling.
